available_assertion.statement: Multiplication by n on an abelian variety of dimension g has degree n^(2g), and degree of genuine isogenies is multiplicative.
available_assertion.objects: An abelian variety A of dimension g and its multiplication isogeny [n].
available_assertion.hypotheses: n is a nonzero integer; the current applications are abelian surfaces in characteristic zero.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such A and nonzero n, and every composable pair of genuine isogenies.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Integral isogenies first; rational quasi-isogenies are treated by the separate denominator calculation.
available_assertion.uniformity: The same degree law holds independently of coefficient prime and is unchanged by field conjugation.
available_assertion.constants: deg([n])=n^(2g), hence n^4 for surfaces; degree is multiplicative.
available_assertion.normalizations: Degree is the rank of the finite locally free map; [-1] is a degree-one automorphism.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No degree is assigned directly to a nonexistent morphism [1/b]. Denominators are cleared before using the source theorem.
available_assertion.limit_order: Apply the multiplication-degree and multiplicativity laws to integral representatives, then prove denominator independence.

available.statement: Every F-algebra automorphism of a finite-dimensional central simple F-algebra B is inner: there is s in B× such that theta(b)=s^(-1)b s for all b in B.
available.hypotheses: B is finite-dimensional central simple over its specified centreF, and theta is an F-algebra automorphism.
available.parameter_range: Any ground fieldF; the application usesF=Q and the quaternion algebraB.
available.normalizations: The conjugating element is invertible in B, not necessarily a unit of a specified order or a genuine integral endomorphism.
available.limit_order: Identify the automorphism of the whole central simple algebra first, then choose the conjugating element.

needed: Correct each geometric isomorphism psi_sigma by a rational endomorphism and clear denominators to obtain a full-B-linear isogeny mu_sigma over the original L; choose mu_1=1.
derivation: The actual geometric endomorphism algebra is B. For each sigma, the given psi_sigma induces the Q-algebra automorphism theta_sigma(b)=psi_sigma sigma(b) psi_sigma^(-1). Applying the full central-simple theorem gives s_sigma in B× with theta_sigma(b)=s_sigma^(-1)b s_sigma. Thus nu_sigma=s_sigma psi_sigma satisfies nu_sigma sigma(b) nu_sigma^(-1)=b for every b inB. It is an invertible quasi-homomorphism. Choose a nonzero integer clearing its endomorphism denominators; mu_sigma is then a genuine isogeny, and multiplying by that central integer preserves full-B-linearity. All relevant Hom groups and endomorphisms are already defined overL, so this operation requires no extension ofL. There are finitely many sigma inGal(L/Q); make these choices finitely, choose identity at1, and inflate as in the manuscript.
incoming: The actual non-CM equality End^0(A_Qbar)=B and the given Q-structure on B.
